Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: conclusion length differs: the 1962 prints "Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate."; the antecedent prints "Per Do- minum. Commuiiio. ib. Semel juravi i"; accents, ae/oe ligatures and word division differ throughout; the antecedent reading is an optical text layer and its pointing cannot be trusted at comma level. Corroboration: 1922 Mame at artifact PDF p. 873, alignment 0.79; 1604 at lines 54422-54430, alignment 0.65 (degraded-latin; corroboration only); 1570 at lines 58248-58257, alignment 0.68 (degraded-latin; corroboration only). Recorded limitation: The 1962 reading was settled on the facsimile page image; the antecedent reading is an optical text layer only and its letterforms and pointing were not verified on a page image (the 1862's images are not available to this lane, and the Mame's were not rendered for this entry). What was NOT checked: the Benziger conformed printing was used only as a boundary check on the extraction, never as a reading; no attempt was made to establish which of several possible loci in the antecedent is the 'original' one, since an order is not a contribution. This oration is one the Missal draws from a Common; the antecedent witness may print it at the Common, at another saint's day, or at both. That is a difference of position, not of words.

propers.name: Postcommunion
propers.text:
Refecti participatione muneris sacri, quaesumus, Domine Deus noster: ut,
cujus exsequimur cultum, intercedente beato Timotheo Martyre tuo atque
Pontifice, sentiamus effectum. Per Dominum nostrum.
